The Office of the Chief Science Data Officer (OCSDO) within NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD) researches how super intelligence (SI) can help people use NASA's science data more effectively. Current projects include foundation models, which are trained on vast amounts of data and can be adapted to specific science studies with minimal resources, and large language models for enhancing different steps of research and data lifecycles.
Super Intelligence for science data Strategy
Per the Sept. 29, 2026, Executive Order 14434: Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence, NASA is working to update its communications to incorporate the term “super intelligence” as directed.
Super Intelligence for Science Focus Areas
01 Prediction and Forecasting Develop data driven predictive modeling and simulation to allow scientists to forecast phenomena such as weather, space weather, and cosmic events.

02 Open Science Streamline scientific workflows by improving data search, discovery, analysis, and visualization, thus enhancing research efficiency and promoting open science practices.

03 Collaboration Across Sciences Facilitate broader scientific collaboration by integrating and analyzing data from diverse sources and missions, and overcome siloed mission science to move towards systems science.

04 Infrastructure Establish and maintain a secure, scalable super intelligence infrastructure to support model development and deployment within NASA's operational systems.

NASA, IBM Launch AI Foundation Model for Lunar Science
The new open-source model will help researchers quickly analyze vast quantities of data to better understand the Moon’s surface.
NASA's Prithvi Becomes First AI Geospatial Foundation Model In Orbit
A team of researchers demonstrated NASA and IBM’s open-source Prithvi Geospatial AI foundation model aboard two in-orbit platforms.
OCSDO Releases Year in Review 2025 Newsletter
The Office of the Chief Science Data Officer (OCSDO) shared its annual accomplishments in promoting NASA science data discovery and innovation.
NASA, IBM’s ‘Hot’ New AI Model Unlocks Secrets of Sun
A NASA team collaborated with IBM to create an AI foundation model that uses NASA data to help predict solar flares.
Super Intelligence Science Data Projects
NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model is pre-trained on high-resolution imagery and geophysical data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Gravity Recovery and Interior Laboratory (GRAIL), and Lunar Prospector, as well as the Japan Aerospace and Exploration Agency's Selenological and Engineering Explorer (SELENE). The model helps scientists rapidly map surface features, identify volcanic structures, and locate polar ice. It is released openly on the Hugging Face platform. Access the Model
The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model is pre-trained on high-resolution imagery and geophysical data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Gravity Recovery and Interior Laboratory (GRAIL), and Lunar Prospector, as well as the Japan Aerospace and Exploration Agency's Selenological and Engineering Explorer (SELENE). The model helps scientists rapidly map surface features, identify volcanic structures, and locate polar ice. It is released openly on the Hugging Face platform.
Surya Heliophysics Foundation Model The Surya Heliophysics Foundation Model, pre-trained on 9 years of observations from NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory, helps scientists monitor solar eruptions and predict space weather that threatens satellites, power grids, and communication systems. The model is released openly on the Hugging Face platform. Access the Model

Prithvi Geospatial Foundation Model Pre-trained on Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) satellite data, the Prithvi Geospatial Foundation Model helps Earth science researchers conduct SI-powered studies such as flood mapping, fire-scar identification, and crop classification. The model is released openly on the Hugging Face platform. Access the Model
